title: The rules runner runs every suite one at a time, with no parallel option
body:
## Summary
tools/run-rules.cjs ran the 94 rulesSuites strictly sequentially (wall 237 s at base, 639 s under four agents) on a 16-core machine, with no way to run them in parallel.

## Description
tools/run-rules.cjs:78-83 (before) awaited runOne() per suite in a for loop. Now --jobs N / RULES_JOBS runs up to N at once (tools/run-rules.cjs readJobs, worker pool), holding each suite's stdout+stderr and printing it whole under its own header; table in list order; default 1 keeps npm test unchanged. Technique: test-harness/suite-partitioning.

## Flow
- director: full run 237 s wall for 215 s of summed suite time
- fix: --jobs N worker pool, buffered output, refuse non-positive N
- harness-rules-test: overlap read from fixture clocks (load-insensitive), red-suite block, refusal

## Expected impact
The director and an operator can cut the gate's wall time on demand; npm test is unchanged. Could break: interleaving if buffering failed (pinned by the red-block case).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - wall time of a rules run
Before: 40964 ms for the first 15 rulesSuites (jobs 1, shared machine)
After: 34654 ms with --jobs 4, same 986 tests and verdicts
Method: probe - real subset both arms; the full list is the director's run
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
tools/run-rules.cjs:78-83 (before): for (const name of list) { ... results.push(await runOne(name)); }
probe: totals ... wall 40964 ms; jobs 1  vs  wall 34654 ms; jobs 4

title: The harness timeout case kills its own green suite on a loaded machine
body:
## Summary
tools/harness-rules-test.cjs set RULES_SUITE_TIMEOUT_MS=1500 for a list that also holds a green suite, so a slow node start under load turned the harness suite red.

## Description
The bound applies to every suite in the list (tools/run-rules.cjs TIMEOUT). Under four agents t-after took 1705 ms and was killed (h-red run, 2026-10-21). Now t-after spends 2 s before its test and the bound is 8000 ms; t-slow (20 s) is still killed. Technique: test-harness/flake-lifecycle (fix the instrument, not retry).

## Flow
- run harness-rules-test while other suites load the machine
- t-after RED timeout after 1500 ms
- fix: deterministic 2 s start, 8 s bound

## Expected impact
The harness suite stops going red on a busy machine for no runner defect. Cost +5 s per run.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - harness verdict under load
Before: red 1 of 2 full runs today; a 2 s-start green suite red at 1500 ms (exit 1)
After: green at 8000 ms (exit 0), t-slow still red
Method: gate - the case red then green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
tools/harness-rules-test.cjs:76 (before): run([write('t-slow.cjs', SLOW), write('t-after.cjs', GREEN)], { RULES_SUITE_TIMEOUT_MS: '1500' })
observed: t-after.cjs  RED ... 1705  timeout after 1500 ms

## Description

title: dev:https serves a lapsed LAN certificate forever
body:
## Summary
tools/desk-dev-https.cjs makes a 365-day certificate and afterwards only checked that the file exists, so after a year (or with a corrupt pem) the phone's HTTPS voice path hits a hard certificate error on every run.

## Description
Before: `if(!fs.existsSync(cert)||!fs.existsSync(key))make();`. Now a certificate with 30 days or less left, or unreadable as X.509, is made again and the run says the phone must re-trust it. New tools/desk-dev-https-test.cjs (scratch cwd, fake interfaces, openssl; skips without openssl).

## Flow
- a 1-day certificate on disk
- npm run dev:https keeps it
- fix: validTo checked via crypto.X509Certificate

## Expected impact
The operator's phone mic path keeps working past a year. Could break: a re-made cert needs one re-trust on the phone (said in the output).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - certificate served after expiry
Before: 1-day cert kept (1.0 day left); non-pem kept; 2 of 4 cases red
After: both remade (>300 days); good cert kept byte-for-byte; 4 of 4 green
Method: gate
Result: better
Gate: none

title: stick-walk/writing.cjs: no PW fallback, fixed desk URL, unasked model call
body:
## Summary
tools/stick-walk/writing.cjs was the one stick-walk tool (of 8) without the `PW || "playwright"` fallback, with http://localhost:3000 hard-coded, and pressing "Get one note" (a model call) on every run.

## Description
Siblings take the desk URL and fall back to "playwright"; writing-panel.cjs is explicit that the walk never presses the model button. Now `<desk-url> <out-dir> [--coach]`, usage exit 2 on missing args, coaching only with --coach.

## Flow
- run with PW unset: TypeError stack
- run against a walk pointed at another desk: still hits :3000
- fix: args, fallback, --coach

## Expected impact
A walk no longer spends a model call or hits the wrong desk by default.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - sibling parity and default spend
Before: no-args TypeError exit 1; 1 hard-coded URL; 1 model call per run
After: usage exit 2; 0; 0
Method: probe - PW unset, no device
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
tools/stick-walk/writing.cjs:1 (before): require(process.env.PW)
:6 p.goto("http://localhost:3000/writing")
:11 getByRole("button", { name: /get one note/i }).click()
grep -c 'process.env.PW || "playwright"' tools/stick-walk/*.cjs: 7 of 8

title: The TypeScript loader's disk cache grows forever
body:
## Summary
tools/ts-load.cjs caches each transpile in <tmpdir>/desk-ts-load keyed by source text and never removes an entry: 1786 entries, 70 MB in 13 days for 241 source files.

## Description
Every edit of every module is a new key. Now, on a miss and at most once a day (.pruned marker), entries older than 14 days are deleted, best effort.

## Flow
- count <tmpdir>/desk-ts-load: 1786 .js, oldest 2026-10-08
- growth ~100-150/day
- fix: daily prune by mtime

## Expected impact
Temp space stays bounded; a live entry pruned is transpiled once more.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - unbounded disk growth
Before: entries never removed (14-day-old fixtures survive a miss; projected ~50k entries, ~2 GB at a year)
After: pruned to a 14-day window; harness case red then green
Method: gate
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: find <tmpdir>/desk-ts-load -name "*.js" | wc -l -> 1786; du -sh -> 70M; older than 10-12: 456, than 10-18: 1224

title: @types/node 26 describes a runtime the desk never runs on (Node 24)
instrument: pin @types/node to ^24 (npm install, network) and run tsc --noEmit on both arms; seed a Node-26-only API call and count whether each arm accepts it
body:
## Summary
desk/package.json:120 declares "@types/node": "^26" (lock 26.6.5) while every workflow sets node-version 24 (10 sites) and the operator runs v24.14.0; no engines field says which Node the desk targets.

## Description
Types for a newer major let tsc accept APIs that throw on the runtime. Fix: @types/node ^24 plus "engines": {"node": ">=24 <25"}; dependabot would need an ignore for majors above the runtime.

## Flow
- grep node-version .github/workflows: 24 x10
- desk/package-lock.json node_modules/@types/node 26.6.5
- a 26-only API type-checks and fails at runtime on 24

## Expected impact
tsc stops vouching for APIs the desk cannot call. Could break: code already using a 25/26-only API (tsc would name it).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - type surface matches runtime
Before: types major 26 vs runtime 24
After: not taken (npm install needs network)
Method: simulation - versions read from lock, workflows and node --version
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none

title: allowedDevOrigins blocks hosts lanHost() sends the phone to
body:
## Summary
desk/next.config.ts:9 allows 10.0.0.*, 192.168.*.* and *.local, but desk/src/lib/session/lan.ts:9-17 ranks all of 10/8, 172.16/12, 100.64/10 and 169.254/16 as phone hosts, plus DESK_PHONE_HOST.

## Description
Two lists of "this machine's LAN address" disagree. A desk on 10.1.4.20, 172.20.x.x (a Hyper-V/office LAN) or a Tailscale 100.x address prints a phone URL Next silently refuses in dev: the page renders as HTML and never hydrates (desk/README.md:156-159). Narrowest fix: append lanHost() (and DESK_PHONE_HOST) to allowedDevOrigins in next.config.ts. It widens the dev-origin allow-list, so it is policy-loosen.

## Flow
- desk on 172.20.1.5: lanHost() -> 172.20.1.5
- phone opens http://172.20.1.5:3000/phone
- Next blocks dev requests from that origin; "connecting..." forever

## Expected impact
Phones on non-192.168 LANs work without editing config. Could break: nothing in production (allowedDevOrigins is dev-only).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - phone pages hydrate on every LAN lanHost picks
Before: 2 of 5 private ranges lanHost ranks are allowed (one only for 10.0.0.0/24)
After: the advertised host is always allowed
Method: simulation - ranges walked against both lists; no dev server in this run
Result: better
Gate: policy-loosen

title: --jobs dispatches in list order; the 26 s suite can end the run alone
instrument: record each suite's ms to <tmpdir>/desk-rules-durations.json, dispatch longest-first; time the full list at --jobs 4 in list order vs longest-first, three runs each, and count verdict differences against jobs 1
body:
## Summary
tools/run-rules.cjs --jobs hands suites out in list order; school-stretch-test (26.2 s) sits at index 44 of 96, so a late start can leave it running alone. npm test and quality.yml still run jobs 1.

## Description
Technique: test-harness/history-driven-partitioning (split by measured duration, longest first). Adopting --jobs in the gate also needs the calc-rules-test parallel card (Approvals) settled first.

## Flow
- full list at --jobs 4
- school-stretch-test starts after ~44 suites
- tail of the run is one worker

## Expected impact
The director's and CI's gate wall shrinks toward sum/jobs. Could break: a shared-state suite under parallel (named by the instrument's verdict diff).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - full gate wall
Before: 237 s jobs 1 (director)
After: predicted ~70-90 s at --jobs 4 longest-first on an idle machine
Method: simulation - list positions and suite times
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/package.json rulesSuites index of school-stretch-test.cjs: 44 of 96
director: school-stretch test 2 25.5 s of 26.2 s

title: A timed-out suite's child processes outlive the runner's kill
instrument: harness case: a fixture that spawns a 15 s sleeper with inherited stdio, RULES_SUITE_TIMEOUT_MS=1500; assert the runner returns within 5 s and the sleeper pid is gone; run on Windows and on the Linux CI runner
body:
## Summary
tools/run-rules.cjs kills only the direct child (child.kill('SIGKILL')); a suite that spawned processes (harness-rules-test, desk-pairing-test, kpi-measure-test do) leaves them running, and on POSIX an inherited stdout pipe can hold the 'close' event open past the timeout.

## Description
Probe on Windows: the runner returned at 1531 ms but the 15 s grandchild lived on. Linux not measurable here. Fix: spawn detached and kill the group (process.kill(-pid)) on POSIX, taskkill /T /F on win32; resolve on exit after destroying the pipes.

## Flow
- suite spawns a child and hangs
- runner times out at RULES_SUITE_TIMEOUT_MS
- orphan keeps running (and on Linux may stall the runner)

## Expected impact
A hung suite costs its timeout and nothing more. Could break: a suite that relies on a detached child (none found).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - processes left after a timeout
Before: 1 orphan per timed-out suite with a child (Windows probe)
After: 0 (to measure)
Method: probe - Windows only
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
tools/run-rules.cjs: const timer = setTimeout(() => { timedOut = true; child.kill('SIGKILL'); }, TIMEOUT);
probe: gc.cjs RED 1530 timeout after 1500 ms; grandchild setTimeout 15000 still running

title: The runner's default suite timeout is 23x the slowest suite
instrument: collect per-suite ms from three loaded full runs (the new slowest-tests line plus the table), set the default to 2.5x the loaded maximum, and re-run the harness timeout case
body:
## Summary
RULES_SUITE_TIMEOUT_MS defaults to 600000 (tools/run-rules.cjs TIMEOUT, also kpi-measure.cjs:71) while the slowest suite takes 26.2 s at base: a hung suite costs 10 minutes of every gate before it is named.

## Description
Under load the director measured 639 s wall for 534 s summed (factor ~2.5); a default near 180 s keeps 2.7x headroom over the loaded slowest suite. The engines-suite hang itself is carded in Approvals; this is the runner's bound.

## Flow
- a suite hangs
- the gate waits 600 s
- then reports a timeout

## Expected impact
A hang costs ~3 minutes instead of 10. Could break: a legitimately slow suite on a very loaded machine (the instrument sizes the bound).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - cost of one hung suite
Before: 600 s
After: ~180 s predicted
Method: simulation - suite times from the director's runs
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
tools/run-rules.cjs:20 TIMEOUT default 600000
tools/kpi-measure.cjs:71 SUITE_TIMEOUT default 600000
